learn.title: v2.1.314
learn.headline: Claude Code now summarizes long idle chats to save tokens.
learn.reason: Shows how long conversations cost tokens and context, and how to manage them; directly relevant to your agent-cost learning.

card.headline: Claude Code now summarizes very long chats left idle
card.gist: In VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab, a very long idle chat now gets summarized. If a short-lived saved copy of the chat has expired, your next message uses the summary.
card.picture: It's like a huge raw events table and a small daily summary table. Your next query reads the summary, not every raw row. The details are condensed, but the main facts carry forward.
card.why_you: Every AI chat or agent you build will grow too long one day. Shrinking old history into a summary is a design choice you will make too.
card.remember: When history grows too long, carry a summary forward.
card.term_meaning: Replacing a long conversation history with a shorter summary, so the model can keep working from it.
card.say_it: When an agent's history gets too long, I compact it into a summary instead of resending everything.
card.follow_up_why: Because a model can read only a limited amount of text per request, called its context window.
card.reality_check: This comes from Anthropic's own Claude Code release notes; it applies to VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab.
card.try_it: In a long Claude Code session, run /compact and read the summary it keeps.

learn.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
learn.headline: Study finds many agent memory systems do worse than plain retrieval.
learn.reason: Shows when fancy memory loses to simple RAG; a strong interview talking point.

card.headline: Study finds many AI memory systems lose to simple search
card.gist: Researchers tested special memory systems for AI agents. In many cases, they did worse than simply searching the raw past conversation.
card.picture: Think of keeping only a summary table and deleting the raw rows. Common questions get faster answers. But a question that needs a deleted detail can no longer be answered.
card.why_you: When you build agents, an extra memory layer is not automatically better. Compare it against plain search of the raw history first.
card.remember: Always test agent memory against plain search of the raw history.
card.term_meaning: What an agent loses when its memory system removes or hides evidence that was in the raw history.
card.say_it: I judge agent memory by net value: its gains over plain retrieval, minus its memory tax.
card.follow_up_why: Because reorganizing or condensing history can drop the exact evidence a later question needs.
card.reality_check: This is the authors' own paper; they say they will open-source the code and results. Reading it is free.
card.try_it: Open the paper's project page and note how they compare memory with plain retrieval.
